title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1970-03-07

ai_review.summary: A fair‑quality audience tape that still delivers a high‑energy 1970 performance – think scorching China > Rider > High Time, a monster Lovelight and a blistering The Other One.
ai_review.review: Despite the inevitable hiss, pops and occasional crowd‑over‑the‑band moments of this AUD recording, the music shines.  The show is praised for its relentless intensity, especially the China > Rider > High Time sequence, the epic Lovelight, and a ferocious The Other One, with most reviewers calling it a must‑listen for Deadheads who can look past the sonic flaws.  Overall the performance outweighs the technical limitations.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviewers (30+) give 3‑5 stars and highlight outstanding musical moments, while repeatedly noting that the audio is only listenable but not pristine; this yields a strong show rating tempered by fair recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical AUD issues – hiss, crackles, splices, occasional crowd chatter louder than the band, and a few drop‑outs.  Still considered listenable for the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers rave about the seamless, high‑octane transitions – especially the China > Rider > High Time jam and the NFA → Drums → Good Lovin' → The Other One → NFA → Lovelight sequence – which give the concert a relentless forward momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice is described as “pretty” and “emotional” on Black Peter; guitar work called fast, furious and burning on China/Rider and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass lines praised for ‘machine‑gun’ intensity into Good Lovin' and driving the NFA/Drums groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for “burning guitar work” that lights up the road during the China > Rider segment.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s vocal power highlighted throughout; occasional organ solos missing but his vocal showmanship is strong, especially on Lovelight.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey and Bill described as “stomping like a tribe” with the drum break considered ‘ON’ by several reviewers.
